title: Moral Psychology Analysis Schema
description: Structured analysis of moral psychology in philosophical arguments. Maps the relation between moral judgment and motivation, classifies internalist/externalist and Humean/anti-Humean positions, tests against canonical counterexamples (amoralist, akrasia), and traces metaethical implications.

analysis_id.description: Unique identifier for this moral psychology analysis run

internalism_classification.description: Classification of the argument's position on the moral judgment–motivation relation

strength.description: Whether the position is explicitly stated, implicitly presupposed, or ambiguous

humean_diagnosis.description: Classification of the argument's theory of motivation

position.description: Whether the argument adopts the Humean belief-desire model, an anti-Humean alternative, a hybrid view, or does not specify

belief_desire_role.description: How belief and desire function in the argument's motivational picture

amoralist_assessment.description: Evaluation of how the argument handles the amoralist counterexample

verdict.description: How the position treats the amoralist

empirical_adequacy.description: Whether the view's treatment of the amoralist is empirically adequate

akrasia_analysis.description: Evaluation of how the argument handles akrasia (weakness of will)

motivational_architecture.description: Structural map of how moral judgment, desire, belief, intention, and action are related

direction_of_fit.description: Direction of fit assignments for each psychological state

causal_chain.description: The 'because' chain from judgment to action in the argument's picture

metaethical_implications.description: Mapping of the argument's moral psychology to compatible and incompatible metaethical positions

compatible_positions.description: Metaethical positions compatible with the argument's moral psychology

incompatible_positions.description: Metaethical positions ruled out by the argument's moral psychology

moral_problem_trilemma.description: How the argument resolves (or fails to resolve) Smith's moral problem trilemma of cognitivism, internalism, and Humeanism
